papers.title: Shared human-machine control of an intelligent bionic hand improves grasping and decreases cognitive burden for transradial amputees
papers.notes: A sensor-equipped prosthetic hand shares control between a user’s EMG signals and a machine controller that helps position the fingers. Tests including four people with transradial amputations found improved grip precision and security and reduced cognitive burden.

papers.title: Gaze, visual, myoelectric, and inertial data of grasps for intelligent prosthetics
papers.notes: The MeganePro dataset combines EMG, gaze, first-person video and inertial measurements from 30 participants without limb loss and 15 people with transradial amputations. A useful resource for studying multimodal intent prediction.

papers.title: Bring Your Own Grasp Generator: Leveraging Robot Grasp Generation for Prosthetic Grasping
papers.notes: A shared-autonomy system combines monocular 3D reconstruction and robotic grasp generation to configure a prosthetic hand during reaching, using the user’s motion to help select a grasp.

papers.title: TinyMyo: a Tiny Foundation Model for Flexible EMG Signal Processing at the Edge
papers.notes: A 3.6-million-parameter Transformer pretrained using masked reconstruction supports several EMG tasks, including gesture classification and hand kinematics regression, and can run on a low-power microcontroller.

papers.title: Agency-Constrained Shared Autonomy for Prosthetic Grasp Selection: A Reproducible Offline Benchmark for Interactive AI in Assistive Robotics
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
papers.notes: An agency budget limits how far autonomous grasp choices may deviate from inferred user intent. The evaluation uses an offline replay benchmark on MeganePro data, not a deployed clinical system.
